title: Untangle rollout routing graph and deprecate legacy config-compat layer
creator: Alicia Park
description: Background: Over the years we accumulated a compatibility layer that maps a series of legacy rollout graph versions (v0, v1, v2) into the current router representation. This shim was originally introduced to preserve backwards compatibility for older admin tools and for a handful of integrations. It now adds significant cognitive overhead, duplicate decision paths, and increases runtime complexity for routing and auditing. The goal of this ticket is to remove the config-compatibility translation layer, collapse multiple rollout-graph variants into a single canonical schema, and provide a migration/compatibility plan so that affected services and admin UI flows are updated with minimal disruption.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical rollout graph schema is defined and documented in the repo (doc/runtime/rollout_graph.md)
The legacy config-compatibility translator is removed from the control-plane service (no runtime translation layer remains behind a flag)
All existing persisted configs in S3/DB are migrated or have migration scripts gated by a dry-run mode
Admin Console reads/writes use the canonical schema and pass e2e smoke tests (no regressions in canary)
Telemetry (rollout decisions, route traces) continues to include human-readable version metadata and matches pre-migration baselines within 1% of traffic distribution
A rollback path exists: we can re-enable compatibility mode (feature flag) within 2 hours if a production regression is observed
migration_steps: Define canonical schema and document mapping rules from v0/v1/v2 to canonical
Add comprehensive unit tests and property tests verifying mapping for edge cases (wildcard routes, legacy predicate combinations)
Ship read-only compatibility layer that emits deprecation warnings to logs + telemetry (2-week observation window)
Run DB/S3 dry-run migration tool to surface transform failures and manual review list
Coordinate frontend (Console) and infra owners to switch writes to canonical schema behind feature flag
Flip read/write to canonical in canary, validate telemetry and rollout behavior, then progressively promote
Remove compatibility translator code and flags after 2 successful production cycles and a post-mortem
risks: Undetected edge-case in mapping could change routing for a small subset of customers (high-severity for Dedicated tenants with strict traffic policies)
Rollback is non-trivial if migrations mutate persisted configs without backups
Console or automation tooling might continue to emit legacy schema leading to intermittent write failures
Team velocity impact: multiple squads need coordinated windows for flips and verification
comments: 2025-02-12 - Alicia Park: Created ticket after follow-up from runtime on-call. Noted that the translator accounts for ~12% of control-plane CPU in staging during peak test runs.
2025-02-18 - Marco Ruiz: Put together initial canonical schema draft in doc/runtime/drafts/rollout_canonical_v1.md. Opened PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289
2025-02-22 - SRE Review (Priya Shah): Suggest adding canary throttles and alert on route divergence >0.5% compared to baseline. Also requested a dry-run migration mode that does not modify objects.
2025-02-25 - Design (Evan Lee): Console changes scoped; will provide updated UI mocks and acceptance criteria by 2025-03-04. Called out edge-case for legacy admin scripts that read deprecated fields.

2025-03-01 - Marco Ruiz: Completed read-only compatibility deploy to staging. Observations: 6 configs (0.06%) failed strict mapping due to custom predicates — added one-off transform script and notified owners. Planning canary flip next week.
notes: The engineering team should treat this as a coordinated cross-team migration. Plan at least two maintenance windows for Dedicated customers where we run migration tasks in read-only validation mode. Post-migration, schedule a 1-week observation window and a short post-mortem listing any manual fixes applied.
